slug: 2026-03-31 Africa we have a data problem

facts.fact: The essay (Data Landscapers, an AI-assisted 54-country compilation) states that rural primary schools track attendance and marks in handwritten 'livro de turma' class registers and that it found no evidence of routine electronic recording at the school; it gives no date, so the published date is used.

The essay states there is no digital entry at school level in rural primary schools: census forms go on paper through districts and provinces to be digitised centrally in Maputo; no count of schools is given and no date, so the published date is used.

systems.tiers: hand-filled paper questionnaires at schools twice a year (enrolment in March, results in December), forwarded through districts to provinces and digitised centrally in Maputo
school: handwritten class registers of attendance and marks, with limited integration with EMIS
school mapping and planning, piloted in some provinces, not fully functional and not used for attendance or learning data

note: The essay's country rows are the author's AI-aided compilation, flagged in the file as not sourced fact; the facts above are what it states and carry that caveat.
